note: Round 5 literature refresh (quoted-phrase queries, sortBy=relevance), targeting the block-bootstrap / multiple-testing front that reality_check.js implements (White RC, Hansen SPA, consistent SPA_c, Romano-Wolf StepM). Purpose: ground the automatic block-length follow-up and confirm nothing newer supersedes the stationary-bootstrap max-t. Headline finds: 0903.0474 ("A note on the stationary bootstrap's variance") explains the larger asymptotic variance of the stationary bootstrap versus other block bootstraps — consistent with the measured size distortion of the RC/SPA bootstrap on i.i.d. noise being driven by block resampling, not the studentization; 1403.3275 ("Convergence rates of empirical block length selectors for block bootstrap") gives the convergence rates for the Hall-Horowitz-Jing and Politis-White block-length selectors, grounding the `blockLength: "auto"` follow-up in docs/TODO.md; 2212.08372 ("On Asymptotic Behaviors of Stepwise Multiple Testing Procedures") grounds the Romano-Wolf step-down asymptotics. Entries are lightly filtered to bootstrap / multiple-testing / data-snooping relevance.
